---
title: Tracking faces, hands, poses and text
description: Turn on the trackers you need, with the models you choose, and read what they found.
---

Every tracker works the same way: enable it with the task bytes and a thread
count, submit frames, read the result. Nothing is on by default, so a session
only costs you what you asked for.

## Faces and hands

```c
goss_session_enable_face_tracking(session, task_bytes, task_len, threads);
goss_session_enable_hand_tracking(session, task_bytes, task_len, threads);
```

The task bytes are the model, and you supply them, so the accuracy and size
trade-off is yours to make. See [bring your own model](/docs/build/models) if
you want to pin them by digest.

`threads` caps the worker. Zero lets the engine pick based on the device. On a
phone, two is usually right for one tracker and badly wrong for three at
once.

If a count is all you need, ask for one:

```c
uint32_t faces = 0;
goss_session_face_count(session, &faces);
```

Or take the whole [perception record](/docs/concepts/perception) when you want
boxes, landmarks and confidences at once.

## Pose

```c
goss_session_enable_pose_tracking(session, task_bytes, task_len, threads);
goss_session_disable_pose_tracking(session);
```

Pose is the most expensive of the three. Turn it on when the feature using it
appears and off when it goes away, instead of leaving it running for the whole
session.

## Text

Text needs three pieces, because reading is really three jobs:

```c
goss_session_enable_text(session,
                        detector, detector_len,      /* where text is */
                        recognizer, recognizer_len,  /* what it says */
                        dictionary, dictionary_len,  /* what is plausible */
                        detect_side);                /* working resolution */
```

The dictionary is optional, but supply one if your domain has a vocabulary:
part numbers, street names, a menu. It's the difference between reading a word
and reading something that looks like it.

`detect_side` is the working resolution for detection. Smaller is faster and
misses small text, so match it to how big text actually is in your app rather
than to the frame.

Recognised text comes back with its position, its confidence, and which line
and paragraph it belongs to, so you can put the layout back together instead of
just collecting words.

## Segmentation

```c
goss_session_enable_segmentation(session, model_bytes, model_len, threads);
goss_session_enable_source_segmentation(session, ...);
goss_session_disable_segmentation(session);
```

The plain one segments the camera frame. The source one segments a named
source, which is what you want when the thing you're cutting out isn't the live
camera.

## Beauty

```c
goss_session_enable_beauty(session, resource_path);
```

Beauty takes a resource path instead of model bytes, because it comes with a
set of resources rather than a single network.

## Enabling several at once

Each tracker is a worker with its own threads. Three of them at two threads
each won't fit a mid-range phone's budget, and you won't get a crash out of it:
you'll get a [degradation ladder](/docs/concepts/degradation) sitting near the
bottom permanently.

Work out what the screen actually needs:

- A face filter needs faces. It does not need pose.
- A gesture control needs hands. It rarely needs text.
- A scanning screen needs text and nothing else.

Enable per screen, disable when you leave, and read the budget back from the
record to check that what you picked actually fits.

## Checking the build can do it

`enable_*` returns `GOSS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED` if this build doesn't have that
subsystem compiled in. Check [capabilities](/docs/concepts/capabilities) once
at startup and keep the answer, rather than finding out feature by feature.
